title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
authors: R. Fielding, M. Nottingham, J. Reschke (IETF)
why_trusted: The IETF Internet Standard that defines HTTP methods, status codes, headers, content negotiation and content coding for all HTTP versions; rfc-editor.org lists it as current and not obsoleted.

title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
authors: R. Fielding, M. Nottingham, J. Reschke (IETF)
why_trusted: The IETF Internet Standard that defines HTTP caches, freshness, validation, Vary and Cache-Control; it obsoletes RFC 7234 and is itself not obsoleted.

title: RFC 9114: HTTP/3
why_trusted: The IETF standard that maps HTTP semantics onto QUIC streams and defines QPACK use, early data and migration notes; not obsoleted per rfc-editor.org.

title: RFC 9846: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3
why_trusted: The IETF Standards Track specification of TLS 1.3 that obsoletes RFC 8446; every browser and server TLS stack follows it.

evidence.venue: IETF RFC, Proposed Standard (Standards Track), July 2026

title: URL Standard (WHATWG Living Standard)
why_trusted: The living standard that defines URL parsing, percent-encoding, host parsing and the origin concept, which browsers implement.

evidence.venue: WHATWG Living Standard, last updated 14 November 2026

title: nodejs/undici: HTTP/1.1 client for Node.js (fetch, cache interceptor, cookies)
why_trusted: The HTTP client that powers Node.js built-in fetch() since v18, owned by the nodejs organization (MIT); 7.7k stars is above the 2,000 niche bar for Node HTTP clients.

title: jshttp/cookie: RFC 6265 cookie parse and serialize for Node.js
authors: jshttp (HTTP working group of the Express ecosystem)
why_trusted: Small, MIT-licensed TypeScript library owned by the jshttp organization that parses and serializes Set-Cookie and Cookie headers per RFC 6265; Express lists it as a dependency; 1.5k stars is above the 1,000 niche bar for cookie libraries.

title: MDN Web Docs: HTTP and web networking
why_trusted: MDN is the browser-vendor reference for the web platform; its HTTP set has guides on caching, redirections (301/302/303/307/308), authentication, range requests, cookies (prefixes), compression, Compression Dictionary Transport, HTTP/1.x connection management (domain sharding), content negotiation, HSTS and mixed content, plus status 429 and Cache-Control references; it also covers the WebTransport, WebSocket and server-sent events (EventSource) APIs, the Priority header (RFC 9218), 100 Continue and 103 Early Hints, the Set-Cookie __Secure- prefix, and the 4KB-per-cookie limit in the cookies guide; the Set-Cookie page defines Expires, Max-Age (Max-Age wins; zero or negative expires at once), session cookies and the SameSite=None plus Secure rule; the HSTS page explains the first plain-HTTP request weakness, max-age, includeSubDomains, preload and lock-in; the mixed-content page lists upgraded and blocked requests; the Certificate Transparency page explains mis-issuance detection and SCTs; the Compression Dictionary Transport page lists Use-As-Dictionary, Available-Dictionary and same-origin limits; the WebTransport page notes the QUIC connection ID persists across networks (Wi-Fi to mobile) (pages read Nov 2026).

title: High Performance Browser Networking
why_trusted: O'Reilly Media book by Ilya Grigorik (Google web performance engineer, W3C Web Performance WG co-chair), with the full text online under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; chapters cover TCP, UDP, TLS, HTTP/1.X, HTTP/2, SSE, WebSocket and WebRTC. Its Optimizing Application Delivery chapter (Optimizing for HTTP/2, Minimize Concatenation and Image Spriting) states the per-request overhead and bundle cache-invalidation trade-offs.
verified_via: https://hpbn.co/ ; https://hpbn.co/primer-on-latency-and-bandwidth/ ; https://hpbn.co/primer-on-web-performance/ (section Browser Optimization: TCP pre-connect, dns-prefetch link hint, Table 10-2 speculative optimization hints) ; https://hpbn.co/transport-layer-security-tls/ (sections Chain of Trust and Certificate Authorities; Let’s Encrypt, ACME) ; https://hpbn.co/optimizing-application-delivery/ (Optimizing for HTTP/1.x; Minimize Concatenation and Image Spriting) ; https://hpbn.co/http2/ (Request and Response Multiplexing; Header Compression)

title: Cloudflare developer documentation (DNS, Cache, Workers, Images)
why_trusted: Official documentation of a major CDN and DNS provider; its DNS docs list A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, CAA, HTTPS, SVCB and NS records and TTL rules, and its Cache docs define cache keys and purge methods. Its Cache docs also give the default cache key (full URL, Origin header, method-override and forwarding headers) and Tiered Cache (lower and upper tier data centers); its SSL concepts page defines a certificate authority. Its 1.1.1.1 FAQ (What do DNS resolvers do?) describes the resolver asking a root server, then the TLD server, then the authoritative nameserver.

title: Learn GraphQL (graphql.org)
why_trusted: The official GraphQL documentation from the GraphQL Foundation (copyright 2026): schemas, queries, mutations, subscriptions, serving over HTTP, caching.

title: Connect RPC documentation
why_trusted: Docs of a CNCF sandbox RPC project that supports gRPC, gRPC-Web and the Connect protocol from browsers over fetch.
